task: Write a due diligence memo on Deel

nimble.claim: Deel co-founder Alex Bouaziz is CEO; co-founder Shuo Wang is Chief Revenue Officer.
Deel appointed former Intuit executive Joe Kauffman as President and CFO in November 2025, signalling IPO intent.
Dan Westgarth is Deel's COO and is a named defendant in Rippling's amended complaint.
Philippe Bouaziz is Deel's Executive Chairman & Chief Strategy Officer; Rippling alleges a 'Bouaziz Racketeering Enterprise' directed by CEO Alex Bouaziz and his father.

Other Deel executives: Yaron Lavi (CTO), Harish Sharma (Chief Risk Officer), DeAnn Work (Global Corporate General Counsel), Anthony Rodriguez (Chief Compliance Officer); Deel built out its compliance bench in 2025 with CRO, CCO and GC hires.
Co-founder Ofer Simon is listed on Wikipedia as a 2019 Deel co-founder but is absent from Deel's current leadership page, with no documented departure.
Deel CEO Alex Bouaziz told Fortune (Nov 2025) that 80% of his leadership team is unchanged since $0 ARR; the workforce grew from 10 to 3,600 per the article.
Deel was founded in 2019 by Alex Bouaziz, Shuo Wang and Ofer Simon via Y Combinator; Bouaziz was 25 at launch and he and Wang met at MIT in 2013.
Deel Series A (May 2020): $14M led by Andreessen Horowitz per Wikipedia; AccessIPOs lists $18.61M at a $63M valuation.
Deel Series B (Sept 2020): $30M at ~$230M valuation led by Spark Capital with Y Combinator and angels; Wikipedia cites $48M, so sources conflict.
Deel Series C (April 2021): $156M with a16z participation, making Deel a unicorn (~$1.14-1.3B valuation).
Deel Series D (Oct 2021): $425M led by Coatue and DST Global at a $5.5B valuation.
Deel raised ~$50M in May 2022 at a $12B valuation (Emerson Collective per Wikipedia); CEO disclosed a $100M ARR rate at the time.
In February 2025 Deel was valued at $12.6B after a $300M secondary purchase by General Catalyst and Mubadala.
Deel Series E (Oct 2025): $300M led by new investor Ribbit Capital with a16z and Coatue, at a $17.3B valuation; proceeds earmarked for acquisitions and native payroll in 100+ countries by 2029.
Deel CEO said in June 2025 it still aims for a 2026 US IPO, dependent on macro conditions; in Feb 2025 he said it was preparing for a potential IPO. No S-1 is publicly available.

Deel is a Delaware-incorporated, San Francisco-based remote-first payroll/HR/EOR company offering EOR, contractor, immigration, HRIS and performance management; it owns ~250 entities and has in-country payroll teams in 130+ countries.
Deel claims 35,000+ customers in 150+ countries and 6,500+ team members (March 2024); competitors include Rippling, Omnipresent and ADP.
Deel named customers per Reuters include ElevenLabs, Nike, Klarna and Shopify; company blog also cites Reddit and Cloudflare; case studies include Revolut, FICO, Puma, Outreach and Zip Co.

Deel (company claim via Reuters) crossed $1B annual revenue run rate in Q1 2025, with revenue up 75% for the 12 months ended April 30, 2025, and EBITDA margin of 16% in Q1 2025; it earmarked a $200-500M M&A budget for 2025.
Deel platform processes payments for 1.5M+ workers in 150+ countries and serves 35,000+ clients (company claim).
Deel acquired PaySpace in March 2024, its second 2024 acquisition, with ~$500M ARR (company claim).
Deel acquired Safeguard Global's payroll division in March 2025 for an undisclosed amount.
Deel acquired London-based rival Omnipresent for around $15M (per a person familiar, Reuters, Oct 2025).
By end of 2025 Deel had acquired 13 companies including Zeitgold, Roots, Paygroup, Legalpad, Capbase, Zavvy, PaySpace, Hofy, Atlantic Money, Assemble and Safeguard Global's payroll division.
Deel acquired Israeli AI cybersecurity firm Clarity in August 2026.
Deel became Arsenal F.C.'s HR partner in Dec 2025 and sleeve sponsor in May 2026.
Deel was named to the CNBC Disruptor 50 (2024) and the top 10 of the Forbes Cloud 100 (2025).
Aggregator ARR.club (unverified) estimates Deel ARR of $1.2B (Oct 2025), $1.4B (Mar 2026, 40K+ customers) and $1.5B (Aug 2026), +19% annualized CAGR.
The DOJ reportedly opened a criminal investigation into Deel over the Rippling spy allegations (WSJ, Jan 23, 2026); Deel said it is 'not aware of any investigation' and would cooperate.
DOJ grand jury subpoenas were reportedly issued in January 2026 in N.D. Cal. as part of the Deel criminal probe.

Unsealed bank records (Calcalist, Nov 2025) show Deel's $6,000 payment to the confessed spy was routed through an account of the COO's wife and arrived 56 seconds later; Rippling asked what Deel disclosed to its auditors.
Deel admitted in court (June 2025) that it instructed 'discreet surveillance' on the manager at the center of the spy case, after its lawyer initially denied it.
Rippling sued Deel on March 17, 2025 in N.D. Cal. alleging Deel cultivated a corporate spy to steal trade secrets, sales pipeline and playbook.

Rippling's amended complaint (June 5, 2025) adds RICO claims, accuses CEO Alex Bouaziz of orchestrating the plot, names Philippe Bouaziz and COO Westgarth as defendants, and alleges Deel targeted at least four other competitors.

Rippling employee Keith O'Brien (Dublin) swore an April 2025 affidavit admitting ~4 months of searching Rippling's Slack and Google Drive for Deel for a €5,000 monthly retainer (dollars, later crypto); he was caught via a fake 'd-defectors' Slack honeypot.
Deel countersued Rippling on April 24, 2025 in Delaware Superior Court alleging Rippling espionage; Deel voluntarily dismissed it in 2026.
On Aug 20, 2025 a court dismissed Rippling's RICO and fraud claims (a 'unified corporate structure, not a distinct RICO enterprise'); trade-secret claims survived.

A February 2026 federal ruling refused Deel's attempts to dismiss or transfer the Rippling case; as of May 2026 the case is in discovery with RICO claims reported as cleared to proceed (conflicts with the Aug 2025 dismissal report).
Damian v. Deel (S.D. Fla., Jan 2025), a receiver's RICO suit alleging AML failures and facilitation of Russia sanctions evasion, was dismissed on Aug 19, 2025; Deel denied wrongdoing.

Deel facilitated $72M+ in payments (40,000+ transactions) for MyForexFunds, which the CFTC accused of a Ponzi scheme, serving 15,664 of its customers (Nov 2021-Oct 2022); Deel said it was under 1% of revenue and froze the account once informed.
Former Deel workers claimed misclassification in March 2023, and California Sen. Steve Padilla asked the state labor agency to investigate in June 2023; Deel denied the allegations.
Deel's DPayments subsidiary held 26 state money-transmission licenses as of early 2025; no SEC wrongdoing accusation against Deel.
Deel said the Jan 2025 complaint was 'deeply inaccurate' and noted a co-filer was reportedly an early investor in rival Rippling.
Deel's financials are unaudited company claims with no S-1 publicly available; post-Oct-2025 ARR comes only from unverified aggregator ARR.club.
Deel company-reported ARR trajectory: $4M (2020), $54M (2021), $100M (2022), ~$500M (2024), $1B run rate Q1 2025.
Deel told Calcalist (Sept 2023) it had $295M ARR, up from $57M a year earlier.
Deel claimed in March 2025 an $800M run rate, $12B+ valuation, and 2.5 years of profitability.
Deel CEO told Reuters (Oct 2025) that monthly revenue crossed $100M for the first time in September 2025, generating ~$15-17M EBITDA; the company says it has been profitable for three years.
Deel headcount grew from 3,000 (Mar 2024) to 5,000 (Feb 2025), 6,500 (Jun 2025) and 7,500 (2025); no layoffs found.
Deel said in March 2024 it had over $500M ARR achieved organically outside PaySpace, 3,000 team members in 100+ countries, and had been EBITDA positive for 1.5 years.
Deel's Glassdoor rating is 4.3/5 from 2,132 reviews, with 83% recommending to a friend and 88% approving of CEO Alex Bouaziz; some reviews cite burnout and communication concerns.
Deel's homepage shows a 4.7/5 rating from 15,401 G2 reviews (company-published).
TechCrunch called the Rippling/Deel affair 'arguably the biggest drama between two HR startups ever'; court documents showed the spy believed men from Deel were following him.
TechStartups retracted its Jan 2025 article on the Deel Ponzi/laundering lawsuit after Deel disputed inaccuracies.

Deel announced a $300 million Series E on 2025-10-20 at a $17.3 billion valuation, co-led by Ribbit Capital, Andreessen Horowitz and Coatue; latest verified priced round.

Deel claims 40,000+ customers as of 2026-10-13.
Deel claimed 35,000 customers and 1.25 million workers as of June 2025; named customers include Reddit, Klarna and Cloudflare.
Deel claimed 35,000+ customers, 1.5 million+ workers and $22 billion in annual payroll processed as of October 2025 (payroll volume is not revenue).

Deel announced a multi-year partnership with Arsenal (2025-12-12); Arsenal is a Deel HR-platform customer.
Deel acquired AI identity-verification/deepfake-detection company Clarity (announced 2026-08-04), its 15th acquisition; terms undisclosed.
Deel claims it exceeded $1.5 billion ARR in H1 2026 and continued profitable growth (company-defined, unaudited).
Deel claimed $1 billion annual revenue run-rate, 75% YoY revenue growth and nearly three years of profitability as of June 2025 (management statements, unaudited).
Deel claimed it hit its first $100 million revenue month in September 2025 and three consecutive years of profitability; profitability basis unspecified.
Deel reported 6,500+ team members across 100+ countries as of June 2025.

Rippling litigation (People Center, Inc. v. Deel, Inc., N.D. Cal. 3:25-cv-02576-CRB, filed 2025-03-17) remains active with filings through 2026-10-14; no liability finding.

Glassdoor as of 2026-10-21: Deel rated 4.3/5 across 2,132 reviews with 83% recommend rate; compensation/benefits 4.0/5, down 6% over 12 months.

BBB shows 17 complaints against Deel over three years and eight closed in the prior 12 months, concerning billing, payroll/funds access, withdrawals and support; unverified by BBB.

TechStartups retracted its Jan 2025 article on the Deel Ponzi/laundering lawsuit after Deel disputed inaccuracies.

Deel facilitated $72M+ in payments (40,000+ transactions) for MyForexFunds, which the CFTC accused of a Ponzi scheme, serving 15,664 of its customers (Nov 2021-Oct 2022). Deel said this was under 1% of revenue and it froze the account once informed.

A Minnesota Commerce consent order dated 2024-05-23 concerns alleged unlicensed cash-advance/lending and money-transmission activity by Deel, as reproduced in the Surge complaint. Terms and penalty are unverified.
Deel's DPayments subsidiary held 26 state money-transmission licenses as of early 2025; there is no SEC wrongdoing accusation against Deel.
Former Deel workers claimed misclassification in March 2023, and Deel denied the allegations.
California Sen. Steve Padilla asked the state labor agency to investigate Deel over worker misclassification in June 2023. Disposition is unverified.
California Sen. Steve Padilla requested a labor-agency investigation of Deel on 2023-07-06, alleging misclassification of its own workers and problematic client advice. Disposition is unverified.

Glassdoor shows Deel at 4.3/5 from 2,132 reviews, with 83% recommending and 88% approving of the CEO. Compensation/benefits are 4.0/5, down 6% over 12 months. Reviews praise remote flexibility, autonomy and learning, and cite intense pace, burnout, compensation/progression and communication concerns.
Deel's homepage shows a 4.7/5 rating from 15,401 G2 reviews (company-published).
G2 shows Deel Payroll at 4.7/5 from 7,288 reviews. Positives are ease of use and fast payments; recurring negatives are high fees, delays and withdrawal issues.

Trustpilot shows Deel at 4.6/5 from 9,680 reviews. Praise covers usability, transfers and onboarding; complaints cover slow support, payout delays, conflicting withdrawal information and policy changes.
BBB shows 17 complaints against Deel over three years, with eight closed in the prior 12 months, concerning billing, payroll/funds access, withdrawals and support. These are unverified by BBB.
Red flag: Review aggregators show recurring complaints about support responsiveness, payout/withdrawal delays and fees, warranting customer-reference checks.
